definition: In this mental health context, first admission refers to a person’s first hospital admission for treatment of schizophrenia. It distinguishes people who are newly admitted from those with previous admissions.

reasons: The packet does not define what “first admission” means (e.g., whether it is the person’s first hospital admission, how it is determined, or what prior admission history means).

The only support in the packet is that the study concerns “first-admission patients with schizophrenia,” without specifying the requested details about hospitalization and distinguishing newly admitted patients from those with previous admissions.

The definition asserts “treatment of schizophrenia” tied to the first hospital admission, but the packet text only describes the trial objective and population generally, not the definitional linkage for the term.
The packet supports a subgroup of “first-admission patients with schizophrenia,” but it does not support the added detail that the admission is specifically “for treatment.”
The distinction from people with previous admissions is not stated in the source; that interpretation goes beyond the packet text.
This term is not itself a diagnosis, so placing it under the diagnosis sense is not defensible from the supplied source.
